challenge.better_approach: Considered deleting the second half of the refusing tooth, since its first half already reads a missing ticket. But it is the only tooth that drives a demo: true ticket to DemoGateRed, so it stays and moves to scratch. Considered polling the live store for the fixture names during the run instead of recording writes, but a write that is unlinked between two polls is invisible to that.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That one patch reaches the judge. It does not: crossing_demo is not run in the proof's process: _require_demo asks it of a scratch CodeMother over the bus (transitions.py:310 ask_inspector, via inspect_wire), and her ticket_file._TICKETS is derived from her __file__, which is the live commons. So patching _TICKETS in the proof alone moves nothing she reads; the scratch store must also be named to her with inspect_wire.launch(ticket_store=...), as test_entry_gate_jurisdiction.py:80-83 does. Measured 2026-11-16 in a scratch dry run: with the patch alone, the refusing tooth reds (she found no ticket); with both, all four pass.
challenge.prior_art: cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_entry_gate_jurisdiction.py:81-99, test_the_rehearsal_lane_is_retired.py:65-72 and test_the_crossing_compares_what_the_inspector_found.py:188 already patch ticket_file._TICKETS to scratch through the one patch point (D10, held by test_light_modules_keep_the_crossing_off_the_inspector_path clause 6). This applies the same move to the three teeth that were missed.
challenge.real_collision: none: the demo gate (ticket demo-gate) is untouched; only where its proof stages fixtures moves.

answers.falsifier: With the build, the new tooth records writes and none falls under the live _TICKETS. On origin/main it reds, naming the fixture writes. The three demo teeth still pass against the scratch store.
answers.how: Add a _scratch_tickets() context manager that saves ticket_file._TICKETS, points it at a TemporaryDirectory's tickets/, enters inspect_wire.launch(ticket_store=tickets) so the scratch CodeMother answering crossing_demo reads the same store, and restores _TICKETS in a finally. Run each demo tooth's fixture writes inside it. crossing_demo derives the validation path from the ticket file's directory (inspector.py:2865), so the scratch store holds both. A red-first tooth wraps Path.write_text, write_bytes, mkdir, touch, unlink and rmdir in an ExitStack while the three teeth run, and reds on any recorded path under the live store or any fixture name standing there.
answers.traces_to: Law 8 and RULE 1: a ticket's proofs measure only their own component, so a proof writes into no record of truth. The live tickets store is one, and this proof was writing into it on every run.
answers.what: test_transitions' three demo-gate teeth read a scratch tickets store patched at ticket_file._TICKETS, and write nothing into the live one.

bullets.text: test_transitions' demo-gate teeth wrote three fixture tickets and a validations/ dir into the real commons tickets store, unlinking them after. That is a record-store write on every run, and under e56a's parallel verdict it races test_v2_migration's glob-then-read.

title: test_transitions' three demo-gate teeth read a scratch tickets store patched at ticket_file._TICKETS, and write nothing
